supported_claims.text: 青 covers both blue and green. Its upper strokes descend from 生, associated with plant growth; its lower part has early forms identified as 丹 or 井. Both the color of growing plants and older sound relationships may help explain the construction. The modern bottom resembles 月, but does not represent the moon.

Sound and meaning analyses overlap: 生 has been read as semantic or phonetic, and the lower 丹/井 forms have different proposed functions. A purely pictorial moon-and-plants story does not explain the evidence.

disagreements.text: The original motivation remains disputed. Plant color is plausible, but it does not settle whether either component was selected primarily for its sound. The disagreement concerns ancient component functions, not whether the modern lower shape happens to look like 月.
